title: Isa, prophet of Allah
hookLine: Muslims honor Isa, son of Maryam, as a great prophet and messenger who healed by Allah's leave
tomorrow: the one who left in anger

cards: Jesus is in the Qur'an. Not in a footnote: the name Isa comes up in surah after surah. His mother has a surah named after her.
His birth, his first words and his miracles are all told. And when Muslims say his name, they add peace be upon him, as they do for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the other prophets.
After three days in the story of his birth, today steps back and asks: who is Isa, for Muslims?

teach.h: AL-MASIH: A WORD AND A SPIRIT.
teach.b: The Qur'an gives him titles. He is al-Masih, the Messiah. He is called a word from Allah, and a spirit from Him.
He was given a scripture, the Injil, the Gospel. One verse names him in a line with Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Muhammad, the five that tradition calls the messengers of firm resolve. Then his miracles.

teach.h: THE BIRD OF CLAY, THE BLIND, THE DEAD.
teach.b: In Surah Al 'Imran, Isa lists them to his people: he shapes a bird from clay and breathes into it, and it becomes a bird.
Then, in Pickthall's translation: “I heal him who was born blind, and the leper, and I raise the dead, by Allah's leave.” Listen for that last phrase, because it keeps coming back.
By Allah's leave, by His permission; in Arabic, bi-idhni llah. It appears again and again when the Qur'an describes what Isa did. The miracles are real, the Qur'an says, and they are Allah's.
Isa is the one they come through. That phrase holds the heart of how Muslims see him: a great and beloved prophet, born of a virgin mother, a healer, and a servant of Allah, not Allah himself.
Here the two neighboring faiths part ways, so it's worth saying plainly who believes what. Christians believe Jesus is the Son of God, that he died on the cross and rose again.
Muslims honor him as a prophet and messenger, and the Qur'an says he was not killed or crucified, though it was made to appear so, and that Allah raised him up.
Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari speak of his return before the end. Both faiths honor him, and they understand him differently.

how: Muslims honor Isa as one of the messengers of firm resolve, say 'peace be upon him' after his name, and read his story in Surahs Al 'Imran, Al-Ma'idah and Maryam.

o: Jesus, honored in Islam as a prophet of Allah
an Arabic word meaning a gift from heaven
a healer's title used in old Arabian towns

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: shaped, breathed on, and it flew

s: Jesus is not mentioned in the Qur'an
Isa is named in surah after surah, and a surah is named for his mother.
the Qur'an credits Isa's miracles to Allah's permission
by Allah's leave, again and again (3:49; 5:110).
Muslims believe Isa is the son of God
Muslims honor him as a prophet and messenger; Christians believe he is the Son of God.

games.q: Isa stands before people who doubt him. he has healed the blind and raised the dead. how does he describe it?
o: I did this by my own power.
I did this by Allah's leave.
games.why: I heal him who was born blind, and the leper, and I raise the dead, by Allah's leave (3:49).

practice: Think of one person who is sick, hurting or worn down right now, and picture them clearly.

Choose words that would help them hear, not advice, something kind, like I'm thinking of you, you're not alone, or I'll bring dinner Thursday. If you pray, you can ask Allah to heal them, since the healing is His.

wordCard.voice: Isa. Jesus, son of Maryam: in Islam, the Messiah, a great prophet and messenger, who healed by Allah's leave.

orig.note: Arabic: Isa, the Qur'an's name for Jesus, son of Maryam.

carryVoice: Your line: by Allah's leave. That closes Maryam and Isa: a vow, a whisper, a messenger, a palm tree, a cradle, a healer. Tomorrow, a man who left in anger.
